preamble: Unrounding and lowering of the close front rounded vowel [y] to the open-mid front unrounded [ɛ] is a regional change, known mainly from Kentish Old English. Before the written records begin, Kentish had already unrounded /y/ to /e/. Most Modern English words go back to the Anglian outcome /ɪ/, but a handful kept the Kentish form, which became Modern English /ɛ/: merry, knell, left and the pronunciation of bury. The long vowel ȳ also became ē in Kentish (see y_to_e).

examples.note: Kentish form; the Anglian /ɪ/ development did not survive in this word.
ME knyllen sat alongside the Kentish e-form, which became the standard.
ME had luft, lift and left; the Kentish left won out.
West Saxon spelling with ⟨u⟩ but Kentish pronunciation with /ɛ/.
